text: No, Hansen and JRC do not contradict each other. Hansen reports 67.7 ha of tree-cover *loss* in 2020, meaning that area transitioned from forested to non-forested by that year. JRC, however, shows *no forest* in 2020, meaning that by the end of 2020, the asset had no remaining forest cover. This alignment suggests that the 67.7 ha loss in 2020 (per Hansen) likely accounted for all the forest on the asset, leaving none remaining—consistent with JRC’s 2020 baseline. The evidence supports no further loss events after 2020, reinforcing that the asset was deforested by year-end 2020.
